questions.q: Why does the combination of resilient equity valuations and Treasury yields hovering near 5% create duration risk for fixed income portfolios?
o: Because high yields depress bond prices, and fixed income portfolios face severe capital losses if term premia adjust further while equity valuations remain high.
Because equities and bonds always move in the exact same direction, forcing investors to liquidate both asset classes simultaneously.
Because the Federal Reserve has already executed the Warsh hike, eliminating all future volatility from the yield curve.
Because corporate earnings revisions are dropping, which forces bond issuers to default on their coupon payments.
questions.e: High yields mean lower bond prices, exposing fixed income portfolios to capital losses when duration risk is high. When Treasury yields hold near 5% alongside strong equities, portfolios anchored in long-duration bonds suffer if central bank pricing shifts. The other options rely on false premises about asset correlations or nonexistent defaults.
